name: Optical Vehicle Collision Geometry
goal: Identify published methods for converting optically reconstructed 3D vehicle geometry, especially structure-from-motion photogrammetry and Gaussian-splat-derived geometry, into collision-ready rigid-body geometry for physics simulation. Prioritize methods that address geometry fidelity, surface reconstruction or mesh generation, collision-mesh simplification and repair, preservation or estimation of mass, center of mass, and inertia, and validation against measured vehicle dimensions or other trusted vehicle reference data.
summary:
Photo-derived vehicle meshes can already support rigid-body collision simulation when their exterior envelope is tessellated adequately, but the literature contains little vehicle-specific end-to-end work linking reconstruction, collision-proxy repair, and validated inertial properties; [Ros15] is the direct simulation precedent, while [Eri13] establishes photo-based vehicle mesh accuracy.

GEOMETRY-TO-COLLIDER PIPELINE.
- Acquire metrically anchored exterior geometry. SfM/photo scanning produces an explicit vehicle mesh [Eri13]; neural reconstruction can improve mesh-detail fidelity relative to tested photogrammetry and LiDAR workflows [Far25b]. For deformed bodies, laser point-cloud surface reconstruction uses undeformed regions and vehicle dimensional references, REPORTING MEAN SIGNED DEVIATIONS OF +1.36 AND -1.14 CM against the original body [Che14].
- Extract or repair a physics representation rather than use rendering geometry directly. Surface-aligned Gaussian splatting supports rapid Poisson mesh extraction and optional joint mesh-appearance refinement [Gue23]. Non-manifold inputs can be converted to volumetric collision proxies without watertight preprocessing [Su26]; collision-aware convex decomposition preserves interior and boundary collision conditions [Wei22].
- TREAT APPEARANCE GEOMETRY, CONTACT GEOMETRY, AND INERTIAL PARAMETERS AS DISTINCT ASSETS. General Real2Sim pipelines jointly infer mesh/collision geometry and inertial parameters from visual reconstruction plus interaction [Pfa25], whereas Gaussian-mesh joint optimization can refine geometry and physical parameters from trajectories [Mor25].

VEHICLE DYNAMICS CALIBRATION AND VALIDATION. Vehicle mass, CG, and full inertia must be measured or independently estimated: INERTIA ERRORS MATERIALLY AFFECT 3-D COLLISION TRAJECTORIES [Mac97]. Measured EV datasets and empirical estimators provide current reference values [Pre24]; InTenso+ supplies pendulum-based mass-property measurement and CAUTIONS THAT SIMPLE ESTIMATORS ARE INADEQUATE FOR ACCURATE DYNAMICS [Gob14]. The most relevant validation hierarchy is: dimensions/surface deviation against trusted vehicle geometry [Eri13, Che14], collider convergence through tessellation and contact-response comparison to established vehicle models [Ros15], then trajectory/displacement sensitivity to independently cross-checked mass properties [Mac97, Pre24].
